text: . In the ongoing 9th Hero Asian Hockey Championship in Jalandhar, India maintained its unbeaten run by defeating Malaysia 4-2. Both teams had remained unbeaten in the championship until India overcame Malaysia today. This was India’s fourth consecutive win in the tournament.In the first match of the day, South Korea thrashed Bangladesh 5-0. This was Bangladesh’s fourth consecutive defeat, while South Korea registered its second win in four matches.The second league match between China and Japan ended in a 2-2 draw.Tomorrow, India will take on South Korea, China will play Bangladesh, and Japan will face Malaysia.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has directed the establishment of Foreigners Regional Registration Offices (FRROs) in all state capitals by next year. Currently, FRRO offices have been established in twenty States.The Home Ministry said that there has been a substantial increase in the number of foreigners visiting India for tourism, medical and education purposes and there is a need to appoint FRROs in all states. The Ministry said, this will ensure service accessibility, enhance regulatory compliance and promote India as an attractive destination. It said, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the government is strengthening the institutional framework for management of foreign nationals through expansion of Foreigners Regional Registration Offices.The Ministry informed that Central government is pursuing the matter of establishing FRRO’s in remaining States namely Bihar, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya. This will help foreigners visiting India obtain various consular services such as visa extension, conversion, immigration compliance and legal safety. The expansion will strengthen local-level institutional capacity, improve coordination with State authorities and facilitate legitimate foreign visitors. The Foreigners Regional Registration Office regulates, tracks and facilitates the lawful stay of foreign nationals visiting or residing in India. It administers post-arrival registration for eligible categories of foreigners and issues a Registration Certificate or Residential Permit upon registration.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the deep depression over East central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal has moved southeastwards and intensified into a Deep Depression today. IMD added that the deep depression is very likely to move nearly southwestwards, and intensify further into a cyclonic storm over east central adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal by early morning tomorrow. It has advised fishermen not to venture into West Central and adjoining Northwest and Southwest Bay of Bengal during the next two days.The Weather Agency has issued an orange colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal tomorrow. Heavy Rainfall is also expected over Coastal Andhra Pradesh during the next two days.The Met Department has predictedthunderstormsaccompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Gangetic West Bengal, Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two to three days.For Delhi, the IMD has forecast a clear sky tomorrow. The maximum temperature in the National Capital will be around 31 to 33 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature will hover around 15 to 17 degrees Celsius tomorrow.

. India once again remained unbeaten, frustrating Malaysia by 4-2 in the 9th Hero Asian Hockey Championship in Jalandhar, Punjab, yesterday.Capt Harmanpreet Singh played a pivotal role in the win. India continues to lead the table at the top spot.Both teams were undefeated in the championship till India surpassed the opponent last evening. This is India’s fourth consecutive win in the championship.In the first match of the day, Korea thrashed Bangladesh by 5-nil. This was Bangladesh’s fourth consecutive defeat. The second league match between China and Japan ended in a draw as both teams hit 2 goals each.Akashvani correspondent reports that it was again Sarpanch Sahib – Capt Harmanpreet Singh – who demonstrated his class with a hat-trick by converting two penalty corners and one penalty stroke into goals.Although Malaysia played an offensive hockey but could not surpassed the defending champion India’s technique and presence of mind on the ground.With today’s results, all four teams qualifying for the semi-finals have been decided.While India and Malaysia had already reached the semi-finals, Japan and South Korea secured their place in the last four. China and Bangladesh, being out of the semi-final race, will play for the 5th position.Today, India will take on South Korea, China will play with Bangladesh and Japan will face Malaysia. Rajesh Bali, Akashvani News, Jalandhar.

. Russian forces have bombed a humanitarian aid centre in Ukraine, killing 26 people, as the United States announced plans to hold fresh peace talks. According to Ukrainian officials, the aid centre was located in a school in the village of Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region. The school had been closed to students because of its proximity to the front line. Instead, it had been serving as a shelter and a weekly humanitarian aid distribution point, where residents who remained in the village gathered every Monday to collect essential supplies.Ukraine’s emergency services reported that two rescue workers and four police officers were among those killed. Five people, including two rescue personnel, were receiving hospital treatment. Regina Kharchenko, secretary of the Zaporizhzhia City Council, said 27 people remained missing. Police officers and emergency responders were working to reach residents believed to be trapped beneath the rubble. Russia had not immediately commented on the reported attack.

. The 35-year-old UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara will end after the Security Council failed to renew its mandate, said UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres.The UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) was established in 1991 to monitor a ceasefire and organise a referendum on self-determination, which never took place due to disagreements over voter eligibility.UN Chief Guterres said November 1 would mark the start of the mission’s liquidation phase, with its assets returned to contributing countries.The decision follows a Security Council resolution last year recognising Morocco’s autonomy proposal under its sovereignty as the most feasible solution to the conflict. Morocco welcomed the decision, while the Algeria-backed Polisario Front expressed concern.

. Kimi Antonelli has created history by becoming the youngest driver in F1 history to be crowned champion after finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.The 20-year-old Italian has secured the title for Mercedes. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won the race as Lewis Hamilton finished second in the Ferrari. Kimi needed only a ninth-place finish at the 71-lap race at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez to clinch his maiden world title, regardless of how Lewis Hamilton and his Mercedes teammate George Russell performed.Starting fourth, Antonelli delivered a composed drive to secure third place despite a red flag following a crash involving Valtteri Bottas and a late Safety Car period triggered by an accident involving Arvid Lindblad.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today highlighted the importance of disciplined speech and mind, austerity, self-sacrifice, and truthfulness. Sharing a Sanskrit Subhashitam today, Mr Modi said that a person whose speech and mind are well disciplined and focused, and whose life is characterised by austerity, self-sacrifice, and truthfulness, attains the highest attainments in life.

. Dhinidhi Desinghu has made history by becoming the first Indian female swimmer to win a medal at the Youth Olympics 2026 at Dakar in Senegal. The 16-year-old clocked 56.27 seconds to finish third behind Croatia’s gold medallist Ana Bobanovic (55.89 seconds) and New Zealand’s silver medallist Alyssa Lawson (56.13 seconds). Earlier, Desinghu became the first Indian female swimmer to qualify for a Youth Olympics final after advancing to the women’s 100m freestyle medal race.Meanwhile, Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada today became only the second Indian judoka to reach the Youth Olympic Games final, assuring herself of at least a silver medal in the women’s 63kg category at Dakar in Senegal. 15-year-old Khushbu stormed into the final with her win against Dounia Berrahoual of Algeria. Khushbu can become the first Indian judoka to win a gold medal in the Youth Olympics if she beats Germany’s Cadet world champion Jolina Reinhold in the final tonight. Thangjam Tababi Devi is India’s lone judo medallist at the Youth Olympic Games. She won a silver medal in the women’s 44kg category in the 2018 edition in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

. India has won 14 medals, including four gold, two silver and eight bronze, at the 46th International Tammer Boxing Tournament held in Tampere, Finland. The Indian contingent finished at the top of the medal tally at the international event, which concluded yesterday.Aarti Dhariyal in the women’s 54-kilogram category, Ankushita Boro in the women’s 65-kilogram category, Arundhati Chaudhary in the women’s 70-kilogram category and Pawan Bartwal in the men’s 55-kilogram category clinched gold medals for the country.Mohammed Hussamuddin in the men’s 60-kilogram category and Jaismine in the women’s 57-kilogram category secured silver medals.The eight bronze medallists for India included Vivek Meena (men’s 65kg), Hitesh (men’s 70kg), Akshay (men’s 80kg), Bobin Chauhan (men’s 90kg), Chetan Choudhary (men’s 90+kg), Tanu (women’s 51kg), Disha Patil (women’s 60kg) and Imroz Khan (women’s 75kg).

. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship has called for developing a network of Centres of Excellence to strengthen India’s skill development ecosystem and ensure quality training for youth.Addressing the Recognition of Excellence – Certificate Awarding Ceremony in New Delhi today, Secretary in the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Debashree Mukherjee highlighted that Centres of Excellence should go beyond imparting skills and also promote innovation, production and practical learning. She stressed the need to develop institutions that can facilitate international mobility of skilled youth through specialised training, including foreign language courses.  Ms Mukherjee said the network would also serve as a platform for institutions to share best practices and learn from each other

. Asian stock markets ended on a mixed note today. South Korea’s Kospi climbed 2.2 per cent, China’s Shanghai Composite rose 1.1 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng added 0.4 per cent. In contrast, Singapore’s Strait Times index lost 1.4 per cent, Taiwan’s Taiex dropped 0.6 per cent, and Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 0.3 per cent.In European markets, Germany’s DAX rose 0.4 per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 added 0.1 per cent, when reports last came in.

. Akashvani will broadcast the recording of the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, delivered by Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, tonight at 9:30 PM. The recording will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani network on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary.Delivering the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, Mr Chouhan said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision, determination and leadership laid the foundation for India’s national unity and territorial integrity. He said that Sardar Patel’s efforts to integrate 565 princely states remain a defining chapter in the country’s history. The Minister emphasised that Patel’s vision of a united India continues to inspire the nation through the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’.Mr Chouhan also said that, inspired by Sardar Patel’s firm approach towards national security and his policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, India has responded decisively to threats from across its borders, including through measures such as surgical strikes.As a tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as independent India’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Information and Broadcasting Minister, Akashvani has been organising the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture since 1955. Over the years, the annual event has served as a rich repository of thoughts, ideas and perspectives on a wide range of subjects. It has also provided an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of India’s diverse cultural heritage and the various dimensions of its developmental challenges.

. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by five paise to close at 94.90 rupees  against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 101.68 in intra-day trade.

. An important meeting of the Defence Ministry’s Consultative Committee will be held in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, today under the chairmanship of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. The meeting will discuss various issues related to national security, including the modernisation of the Indian Armed Forces, the use of indigenous defence equipment and emerging military technologies.The meeting is also expected to deliberate on security preparedness along the western border, strengthening the operational capabilities of the armed forces and measures to address future security challenges. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, along with several Members of Parliament from the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, has reached Jaisalmer to attend the meeting. Senior officials from the Defence Ministry and the armed forces will also participate in the meeting.

. The government today launched the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards to recognise outstanding startups across the country. The awards recognise not just commercial success but also social impact, sustainability, and scalability. Launching the awards in New Delhi today, DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh said that startups can apply under 20 sectoral categories. He said that in addition, there are three special categories for women, students, and the North Eastern region. He added that the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade is at the forefront of driving reforms to promote startups. Mr Singh also emphasised the need for more private initiative to bring more startups in the country. He expressed hope that the awards would further boost the startup ecosystem in the country. The Secretary highlighted that the award covers a wide range of domains including agriculture, fintech, aerospace, health, education, and accessibility, among others. The applications for the award will remain open until 20 November this year.In line with the Government’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and the goal of a five-trillion-dollar economy, Startup India supports startups through initiatives such as startup recognition, tax exemptions, regulatory ease, funding access, and capacity building. Launched in 2016, Startup India has transformed India’s entrepreneurial landscape, fostering innovation and empowering youth, women, students, and first-time founders, particularly from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Over two lakh 25 thousand startups have been recognised by DPIIT so far.

In the ongoing 9th Hero Asian Hockey Championship, India thrashed South Korea by 8-0 and registered its 5th consecutive dominated win today.Earlier, the first match of the day between China and Bangladesh ended in a draw as both the teams hit one goal each against each other through penalty stroke and penalty corner.In the second match, Japan defeated Malaysia by 2-1. Akashvani’s Jalandhar Correspondent reports that today is the last day of pool-stage fixtures at the Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar.Tomorrow is a rest day. From November 4th, the action will move to Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium in Mohali for semi-finals and final. Akashvani’s all FM Rainbow Channels along with the Primary Channel of Akashvani Jalandhar are broadcasting India specific matches live.

. In badminton, veteran Indian shuttler HS Prannoy and emerging women’s singles player Tanvi Sharma will lead a depleted Indian contingent at the Korea Open 2026, with several of the country’s top players opting out of the BWF Super 500 tournament beginning today at Jinnam Stadium in South Korea. India will be without two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu, men’s doubles stars Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, and the ace men’s singles shuttler Lakshya Sen.Prannoy will be India’s sole representative in the men’s singles after Sen’s withdrawal. The former world No. 6, currently ranked 38th, will open his campaign against South Korea’s Asian Games bronze medallist Yoo Tae-bin. In the women’s singles, Tanvi Sharma and Anmol Kharb will carry India’s hopes in the main draw. Malvika Bansod and Ashmita Chaliha, were also part of the women’s singles draw but have withdrawn from the competition. India’s men’s doubles representation will be limited to Arjun Reddy Pochana and Achutaditya Rao Doddavarapu, who will begin their campaign in the qualifying rounds. In women’s doubles, Ritika Thaker and Sonali Singh will represent India, while Dhruv Rawat and Maneesha K will compete in the mixed doubles main draw.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that the government will continue to prioritise capital expenditure to sustain India’s growth momentum while ensuring fiscal discipline. Speaking at HSBC India’s Third Annual Financial Inclusion Gathering in Mumbai, Sitharaman said capital expenditure had delivered good results over the past four to five years through its multiplier effect and would remain an important part of the government’s growth strategy.Addressing the balance between welfare commitments and fiscal consolidation, the Finance Minister highlighted the role of government schemes in improving access to basic services, including food security, housing, sanitation, drinking water and healthcare insurance. Sitharaman also identified credit access, insurance and pensions as priorities for the next phase of financial inclusion. She reiterated the government’s goal of achieving insurance coverage for all by 2047 and said credit access was important for people seeking to start or expand businesses. On employment and skills, she said the government wanted every district to have AI training-capable centers to prepare young people for AI-enabled jobs and address the gap between industry requirements and the skills of graduates.

. Secretary (West) in the External Affairs Ministry Sibi George has underscored the Commonwealth’s need to focus on tangible, people-centric outcomes, including democratizing technology for development. The Secretary was addressing the Pre-CHOGM Commonwealth Foreign Ministers Meeting in St. John’s, Antigua and Barbuda ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM). He also focused on strengthening climate action and disaster resilience, championing reformed multilateralism, among others, to advance the Commonwealth’s shared interests and values.

. The United States is gearing up for its midterm elections today, with voters set to decide which party will control Congress and shape the political future of President Donald Trump’s administration. The elections will determine whether Trump’s Republican Party retains control of Congress or the opposition Democrats gain ground, potentially affecting the president’s ability to push forward his legislative agenda.All 435 seats in the House of Representatives will be contested, along with 35 of the 100 seats in the Senate. Of the 35 Senate seats up for grabs, Democrats currently hold 13, while Republicans hold 22. To secure a majority in the Senate, Democrats need to reach the 51-seat mark. Voting will take place across all 50 states, with polling stations opening between 6 am and 8 am local time, depending on the time zone. The ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran, along with the state of the American economy, is expected to remain among the key issues influencing voters as they head to the polls.

. NITI Aayog today launched the India Science and Technology (S&T) Scoreboard to assess the scientific and technological performance of States and Union Territories across the country in New Delhi today. The scoreboard was launched by NITI Aayog Vice Chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri.The platform aims to provide a comprehensive picture of India’s science and technology ecosystem through key indicators, including research and development expenditure, scientific publications, citations, patent applications and technological innovation. The platform covers 36 States and Union Territories and provides data and insights to support evidence-based policymaking.The initiative is expected to promote collaboration between state universities and centrally funded research institutions, encourage healthy competition and strengthen India’s research and innovation ecosystem in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.Speaking at the event, Ashok Kumar Lahiri said that the scoreboard is not merely a ranking exercise but a platform to help states understand their strengths and gaps and align their developmental priorities with science, technology and innovation. He also emphasised the importance of translational research, stating that fundamental research must translate into innovation and reach the factory floor. He called upon states to take ownership of scientific and technological development and strengthen their innovation ecosystems.

. The country’s first Road Safety Research and Training Centre is being set up at Saswad in Pune district. The project is being developed on around 25 acres of land. State Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik recently inspected the ongoing work. The centre will house an Automated Vehicle Inspection Centre, a driver skills testing track and a Road Safety Training and Research Institute.Automated systems will be used to inspect vehicles for brakes, lights, suspension and pollution levels. Modern technology will also be used to assess the driving skills of applicants. The facility is expected to make vehicle inspections and the driving licence issuance process more transparent. Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik has directed officials to ensure that the centre is developed in accordance with international standards and equipped with state-of-the-art technology.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, it is a matter of pride for 140 crore Indians that the country has so far managed  global challenges ranging from the COVID-19 pandemic to the West Asia crisis  effectively and sustained high growth. Addressing the gathering after inaugurating four-day Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, the Prime Minister said the global economy has witnessed unprecedented crises over the past few years and the West Asia crisis is still continuing.  He said that this global crisis has sent a clear message that energy security is directly linked to economic security. He said, the future of energy security lies in clean energy.Prime Minister Modi said, today, more than 50 per cent of India’s installed power capacity is based on non-fossil fuel sources. He said, India is firmly working towards achieving the target of 500 GigaWatt. Mr Modi highlighted that fossil fuel reserves are limited, while the potential of renewable energy is unlimited, and every region and country can benefit from it.Prime Minister Modi said, India is among the top three countries in solar and renewable energy sector. He added that this new phase of the solar revolution is not just about adoption but also depends on innovation. Mr Modi highlighted that in the last 12 years, more than 44 thousand government buildings have been connected to solar energy, resulting in savings of about seven hundred crore rupees annually. The Prime Minister stressed on the need to connect every government building, school, college, hospital, street-lighting system to solar energy.Prime Minister Modi said that farmers across the country are also benefiting from the PM-KUSUM scheme. He said, through this initiative, more than 30 lakh farmers have been provided with solar-powered irrigation facilities. Mr. Modi stated that estimates indicate that farmers can save approximately one lakh rupees annually by using solar-powered pumps.On the occasion, New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi said that the renewable energy sector has attracted investments worth 67 billion dollars during the past two years. He said, under the guidance of Prime Minister Modi, India’s non-fossil fuel-based installed capacity has crossed 310 gigawatts, compared to 200 gigawatts in September 2024. Mr Joshi added that Foreign Direct Investment in the sector has also reached 6.2 billion dollars, reflecting strong investor confidence in the sector.The summit has been being organised by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy with the theme of Invest. Innovate. Inspire. Participants from more than 130 countries, including over 40 ministers, are attending the summit. It has brought together policymakers, investors, financial institutions and industry leaders to promote clean energy investments, technological innovation and international partnerships. In this summit, Australia, Denmark, the European Union, France, Germany,  Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom is participating as country partners. Thirteen States and Union Territories are showcasing their renewable energy potential, investment opportunities and manufacturing capabilities.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24-carat gold shed 1.8 per cent to 1,37,524 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, silver lost over 0.7 per cent to 1,79,972 rupees per kilogram.

. Australian cricketer Glenn Maxwell has announced his retirement from international cricket, bringing the curtain down on a remarkable 14-year career. One of the most destructive and unconventional batters of his generation, Maxwell leaves behind a legacy built on breathtaking strokeplay, match-winning performances and an ability to turn games around almost single-handedly.The 38-year-old represented Australia across all three formats, playing seven Tests, 149 One-Day Internationals and 130 T20 Internationals. He scored 3,990 runs in ODIs, 2,897 in T20Is and 339 in Test cricket. He also claimed 136 international wickets, establishing himself as a valuable all-round option in Australia’s white-ball teams. Maxwell’s international journey began with his ODI debut against Afghanistan in Sharjah in 2012. He made his T201 debut against Pakistan in Dubai in September that year before earning his Test cap against India in Hyderabad in March 2013.

. Eminent neurosurgeon and Padma Shri awardee Professor Dr Ashok Kumar Mahapatra passed away last night while undergoing treatment at AIIMS, New Delhi. He was 74. He was a distinguished medical professional from Odisha whose contributions to neurosurgery brought recognition to the country. Dr Mahapatra was the founding Director of AIIMS Bhubaneswar and also headed the Department of Neurosurgery at AIIMS, New Delhi.He gained national prominence for leading the historic surgical team that successfully separated the conjoined twins, Jaga and Balia, in a landmark operation at AIIMS in 2017. He also served as Director of Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences, Lucknow, and Vice-Chancellor of Siksha ‘O’ Anusandhan University, Bhubaneswar. He was conferred the Padma Shri in 2025 for his outstanding contribution to medicine.Several political leaders, members of the medical fraternity, academicians and people from different walks of life expressed grief over the demise of Dr Ashok Kumar Mahapatra. They recalled his outstanding contribution to neurosurgery, medical education and the development of AIIMS Bhubaneswar.

. Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri will undertake a 2-day official visit to Nepal from November 4 to 5 at the invitation of Nepal’s Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai.The visit will provide an opportunity for the two sides to review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on matters of mutual interest.During the visit, Mr Misri will hold bilateral discussions with his Nepali counterpart, Amrit Bahadur Rai. The discussions will focus on further strengthening the longstanding, close and friendly relations between the two neighbouring countries.Mr Misri is also scheduled to pay courtesy calls on senior Nepali dignitaries during his stay in Kathmandu. He will depart for New Delhi on November 5.The visit is part of the regular high-level exchanges between India and Nepal, reflecting the importance both countries attach to their bilateral relationship.India and Nepal share longstanding historical, cultural and people-to-people ties, with cooperation spanning trade, connectivity, energy, development partnership and other areas.<>

. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri today held meetings with several senior UAE officials and dignitaries in Abu Dhabi, discussing cooperation in key sectors including diplomacy, culture, tourism, finance, investment as well as regional developments. On the second and final day of visit today, Foreign Secretary Misri met Chairman of the Abu Dhabi Department of Culture and Tourism, Mohamed Khalifa Al Mubarak.The meeting explored closer institutional linkages and fresh avenues for cooperation in cultural and creative exchanges, including the proposed House of India, as well as tourism. He also interacted with Chairman of the Abu Dhabi Department of Finance and Managing Director and Group CEO of L’IMAD Holding Company, Jassem Mohamed Bu Ataba Al Zaabi. The discussions focused on prospects for scaling up economic engagement, enhancing investment flows and building long-term commercial partnerships that benefit both economies.Earlier, Mr Misri held discussions with UAE’s Minister of State for International Cooperation and Special Envoy for India, Reem Al Hashimy, in Abu Dhabi and reviewed the India-UAE relations across various sectors and explored new avenues of cooperation. They also exchanged views on regional and global developments.The visit reaffirms strong strategic ties between India and the UAE and the commitment of both sides to further strengthen their partnership.

. Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today highlighted that India’s civilizational consciousness will offer valuable guidance in dealing with present day challenges in the country. The Minister stated this at the book launch of Timeless India: Protection and Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the leadership of the Prime Minister in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat said that this book offers a unique perspective on the initiatives undertaken by the government to safeguard and revive India’s rich cultural heritage. He emphasised that preserving and revitalising this legacy is essential not only for safeguarding the country’s historical identity but also for shaping its future.This book is written by Former Rajya Sabha Member Tarun Vijay and  published by Indira Gandhi National Centre of Arts and Surbhi publication.

. Global crude oil prices shed more than four per cent today as renewed talks between Iranian and Qatari officials raised hopes of diplomatic progress in easing US-Iran tensions.Brent crude was trading 4.4 per cent down at 108 US dollars and 46 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 4.5 per cent lower at 99 US dollars and 38 cents per barrel, at the time of writing this report.

. Indian Railways has announced 1,265 vacancies for Station Master posts across various Railway Recruitment Boards and zones, opening up new employment opportunities for graduate candidates. The Railways Ministry said that in an important recruitment-related decision, the Railway Board has prescribed that Station Master recruitment will be notified separately from 2026 onwards. The dedicated recruitment process provides candidates with a specific notification covering eligibility requirements, examination procedures and vacancy distribution for the post. The online application window will remain open till 25th of next month. Candidates are advised to review the detailed eligibility conditions, vacancy distribution and application instructions before submitting their forms. The recruitment reflects Indian Railways’ continued efforts to provide career opportunities to eligible candidates while strengthening its operational workforce.

. Garment workers’ demonstrations continued for the second consecutive day in several industrial areas of Bangladesh, including Dhaka, Gazipur and Ashulia, demanding an increase in the minimum monthly wage, an end to blacklisting and the reinstatement of dismissed workers.In Gazipur, hundreds of workers blocked several points of the Dhaka-Tangail highway, causing traffic congestion stretching many kilometres. The government deployed 10 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel alongside police and other law enforcement agencies to maintain order in the industrial areas.In Ashulia, police fired tear gas and used water cannons to disperse protesting workers attempting to block highways. Demonstrations were also reported in Dhaka’s Mirpur area, where police stopped workers from marching towards Mirpur-10.The unrest follows Sunday’s violent demonstrations, which witnessed clashes, vandalism and road blockades. At least 529 garment factories in several industrial areas had declared holidays amid the disturbances.Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed held a meeting with garment industry representatives on Monday, warning that those involved in violence and sabotage would face strict action. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has also directed authorities to protect workers’ interests while ensuring uninterrupted production and exports.
